scopeReview: CED CHA-4.D.1–2 and CHA-4.E.1: interpret and compute accumulation/net change in applied contexts, including units, initial values and physical validity. No unrelated question/resource import or BC technique.
varietyReview: Tank balance, spatial mass density, maximum stored amount, actual occupancy-rate graph, nonuniform production table, derivative sign versus state sign, marginal cost, zero net change versus variation, nonzero-time charge datum, arrivals versus average rate and a physical emptying constraint. Six original-data integral/graph/table corroborations and five exact contextual reviews.
repetitionReview: Each prompt and all four options were read separately; distinct tasks/contexts within this set. Cross-topic exact duplicates checked by validator. Semantic similarity and AP difficulty remain judgment calls, not proven by an automated score.

questions.independentReasoning: Independently compute total inflow 28 liters and total outflow 8 liters. The balance 30+28−8=50 confirms the signed-rate integral. Both rates are measured per minute, so integrating over minutes produces liters.
optionReview: This is the net change without the initial 30 liters.
This includes inflow but ignores the outflow.
This subtracts the net increase instead of adding it.
The net rate is 3+t, whose four-minute integral is 20 liters.

questions.independentReasoning: Check dimensions independently and compare the constant-density special case ρ=2 grams/cm: the integral gives 20 grams, while average density is 2 grams/cm and length is 10 cm. These distinct results rule out confusing a total with a normalized average.
optionReview: Density per unit length times small lengths accumulates mass.
Average density additionally requires division by length 10.
The variable is position, not time, and no time rate is supplied.
Integrating a nonconstant density does not simply recover length.

The accumulation V(t)=2−t stays nonnegative until it first reaches zero at t=2.
